150fbf92.task:
Comprehensive reconnaissance and attack-surface mapping of the target web application: https://www.hritish.space

This is BLACK-BOX recon — no source code available. Your job is mapping ONLY (do not attempt exploitation, injection, or vulnerability validation; just note observations).

Deliverables (save artifacts under /workspace/recon_hritish/ and summarize in your completion report):
1. Fingerprinting: exact HTTP response headers, server software + versions, TLS certificate details, CDN/WAF presence (wafw00f), tech stack (frameworks, CMS, libraries) from headers/HTML/meta. Note any security headers present/missing.
2. Crawl: use katana and/or gospider (bounded: depth ~4, time-limited) to enumerate all reachable pages, endpoints, forms (fields/actions/methods), query parameters, and API-looking paths under https://www.hritish.space. Use httpx to probe interesting paths. Save a deduplicated endpoint list.
3. JS analysis: collect all JavaScript URLs, fetch them, scan for API endpoints, hardcoded secrets/keys, interesting strings. Save findings.
4. Fuzzing: run ffuf with a good wordlist (place wordlists under /home/pentester/tools/wordlists if you need to download one, e.g. common.txt / directory-list-2.3-small) against the host for directory/file discovery, and run arjun for hidden parameter discovery on the main page and any dynamic endpoints. Keep it bounded (a few hundred requests/sec tops, short lists) and record only interesting hits (200/301/302/403/500 etc. with sizes).
5. Network: resolve www.hritish.space; run a bounded naabu/nmap scan (-T4, top ports or -p 1-10000, -sV on open ones) against the resolved IP ONLY if it belongs to the target's hosting (verify hostname first). Record open ports/services/versions.
6. Subdomains: passive subfinder on hritish.space parent domain (informational only — do NOT actively probe other hosts beyond noting what exists; report them so the orchestrator can decide scope).
7. Behavior notes: how the app responds to 404s, redirects (http->https, www->apex?), cookies set (names, flags), any error messages that leak internals.

Constraints: keep TEST traffic strictly against www.hritish.space (and the apex host only if it directly serves the same app). Do not launch heavy brute-force or volumetric scans. Keep raw craw/fuzz output tidy (delete bulky intermediate files once extracted). Use the Caido proxy history (caido_api list_sitemap is fine) only as secondary source — do your own crawl.

Report: structured summary — endpoint tables, tech stack, host/ports, JS findings, params, forms, cookies, security headers, interesting observations — and the location of saved artifacts.

df884d45.task:
Browser-based client-side verification of https://www.hritish.space (a static personal portfolio on Vercel). Prior recon (artifacts in /workspace/recon_hritish/) found: static single page, no APIs/forms/params; Vercel Firewall challenges non-browser clients; /main.js is 11.4 KB of DOM animation code with no reported secrets/endpoints; ffuf hinted 3 paths (/wedding /news /newreply) that could not be verified behind the challenge.

Use agent-browser with your OWN session (e.g. --session browser-verifier) so you're not sharing the default browser. Do NOT navigate to any external domain — only www.hritish.space paths.

Tasks:
1. Open https://www.hritish.space, snapshot the page, and enumerate every link/href on the page (internal and external, just list them).
2. Verify real status of /wedding, /news, /newreply by visiting them in the browser (challenge should auto-pass for a real browser): record what renders (real 404 vs a real page). Also try a couple of non-existent paths (/asdf12345) as a baseline.
3. Fully review the saved /workspace/recon_hritish/main.js for client-side XSS sinks: innerHTML, outerHTML, insertAdjacentHTML, document.write, eval, Function(, setTimeout/setInterval with strings, location.hash/query reads, localStorage/sessionStorage reads, URLSearchParams usage, dynamically creating script tags, any use of user-controllable input. Report any sink that processes untrusted/attacker-controllable data.
4. Check URL-parameter behavior: navigate to e.g. https://www.hritish.space/?x=zzqb1ref — does the page reflect the value anywhere in DOM? (report only if reflected)
5. Test clickjacking-adjacent reality: after page load with the browser, confirm X-Frame-Options/frame-ancestors headers are absent AND check whether the main page contains any state-changing or sensitive actions (it should be purely static) — informational only.
6. Also verify that the page renders no forms/inputs/buttons that submit anywhere (snapshot -i).

Report: for each task — what you found with concrete evidence (URLs, header values, main.js sink audit table: line → sink → data source). Save any useful notes under /workspace/recon_hritish/. Do NOT attempt to exploit anything; unreported observations only. Do not file vulnerability reports — you're a verification leaf agent.
